reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that synthetic corpus composition impacts zero-shot forecasting performance more than generator selection alone. The 'don't pick' principle emerges because generator variance can exceed 2× between top performers (e.g., KernelSynth vs. ETS for Chronos-T5-Mini). Equal-weight mixing stabilizes performance by averaging out idiosyncratic generator biases. This aligns with information-theoretic principles where ensemble methods reduce entropy in prediction distributions. In GSE context, this translates to using Mixed11 as a foundational kernel for temporal reasoning, while GSI leverages it for calibrated uncertainty bounds via conformal prediction. The failure mode occurs when generic generators lack domain specificity—such as modeling score progression or injury timing—which necessitates sports-native generator design. These generators must be embedded into the Mixture protocol to ensure that the synthetic corpus reflects true temporal complexity rather than just statistical mimicry.
